title: Declare compatibility-delta protocol and pin-exception workflow for new community variants
creator: Priya Nair
description: Define an operational protocol (compatibility-delta) and an exception-based pin workflow to clarify how newly submitted open/community model variants are classified, temporarily admitted, and either soft-pinned, fully pinned, or rolled back. This PRD clarifies acceptance criteria, telemetry signals, console surface changes, and rollout steps so PM/Eng/Design share a deterministic path for ambiguous submissions.
background: We repeatedly see ambiguity when community model submissions differ only in tokenizer, minor opset, or fused-kernel behavior. Current intake guidance is fragmented across PRDs and intake notes, causing inconsistent pin decisions, runtime failures on some SKUs, and developer confusion about fallback behavior.
problem_statement: New open-model variants occasionally cause runtime incompatibilities (subtle OOMs, kernel errors, or tokenization drift) that are hard to detect at intake. There's no standardized delta signal describing the magnitude/type of incompatibility, nor a formal exception workflow to admit variants with mitigations (e.g., temporary soft-pin, alias mapping, or restricted-serving tiers). This leads to reactive rollbacks and customer-facing incidents.
goals: Create a Compatibility-Delta (CD) protocol: a small, machine-readable tagset that describes delta types and severity
Define a pin-exception workflow for admitting variants that need mitigations (soft-pin, alias, runtime guardrails)
Specify acceptance tests (runtime probes + telemetry) that must pass to graduate from exception -> soft-pin -> full-pin
Add console indicators and intake UI fields to surface CD tags and recommended mitigations
Ensure E2E telemetry (errors, latency, unit-cost delta) for admitted exceptions is tracked and regularly reviewed
non_goals: Rewriting the entire model catalog taxonomy (out of scope for this ticket)
Automatic pin decisioning via ML in this phase (we will design signals, not build auto-decision)
Immediate changes to billing models or pricing
success_metrics: Reduce number of emergency rollbacks for new community variant ingests by >= 60% within 3 months of rollout
Time-to-decision on ambiguous submissions (submit -> classification) <= 48 hours for 90% of cases
At least 90% of exceptions have a documented mitigation and telemetry dashboard linked in the intake entry
Console surfaces show CD tag and mitigation recommendations for 100% of exception-classified variants
requirements: Design and publish a Compatibility-Delta schema (CD v1) documenting delta_type, severity, source_hint, and recommended_mitigation fields
Add intake UI: new dropdown to capture submitted author’s delta_hint + auto-suggest from lint/probe output
Runtime: add a short runtime sanity probe harness that can be run against a model variant during ingest (tokenization check, small-generation smoke test, key KV cache behavior check)
Catalog API: attach CD tags to model entries and make tags queryable via existing catalog endpoints
Pin-exception workflow doc: steps for Triage -> Exception Admission (soft-pin) -> Monitoring -> Graduation or Rollback
Telemetry: add dedicated dashboards for exception-classified variants showing error rate, tail-latency, memory OOMs, and cost deltas
Console: visual flags (orange/yellow/red) and a one-click guardrail toggle to restrict serving to dedicated-only or to enable slower conservative kernels
Define a weekly intake review cadence: intake owners + runtime SMEs to review open exceptions and trigger graduation/rollback decisions
acceptance_criteria: CD v1 schema published in docs + linked from intake UI help text
Probing harness available as a CI job that returns a standardized probe report JSON for each submission
At least one example of an admitted exception (soft-pin) in staging with telemetry wired and a dashboard link in the intake ticket
Console shows CD tag and mitigation recommendation for every exception entry in the staging catalog
Telemetry alerts created for two key signals: sudden error-rate increase (>3x baseline) and memory OOM spike (>10% of requests) for exception-classified models
Runbook published that defines rollback criteria and owner assignments for emergency cases
Cross-functional sign-off: PM, Runtime Eng, DX (Console), and Security on the protocol and mitigation surfaces
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging, 2 weeks): implement CD v1 schema + probing harness + console flags in staging only
Phase 2 (pilot, 4 weeks): admit up to 5 community variants using exception workflow. Monitor telemetry daily and iterate
Phase 3 (gradual rollout, 4 weeks): enable intake UI for all community submissions; require probe report for admission. Train intake reviewers
Phase 4 (GA): publish docs, teach internal intake process, deprecate old ad-hoc checklist
dependencies: Catalog API change to accept CD tags - ENG-51012
notes: We intentionally call it 'Compatibility-Delta' to emphasize we capture deltas vs a baseline rather than attempt to exhaustively enumerate all failures.
Severity buckets should map to conservative runtime defaults: none/low -> no change, medium -> soft-pin + guardrail, high -> block or dedicated-only serving
Consider adding a short TTL for soft-pins (e.g., 90 days) after which intake must revalidate or graduate the variant
Need to confirm legal/OSS licensing implications for storing community weights metadata (Security/Legal check)
Open question: who can authorize a soft-pin for customer-facing GA: intake owner or runtime on-call? Propose intake owner with runtime ratification.
